newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's downgrades Sumitomo Corp's debt to A2.
newsitem.headline: Moody's downgrades Sumitomo Corp's debt to A2.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday that it had downgraded its rating of the long-term debt of Sumitomo Corp and its units to A2.
Moody's said it had confirmed the Prime-1 short-term ratings of Sumitomo and its unit.
The rating actions reflected both the immediate and long-term implications of the company's substantial copper trading losses for its operating franchise and financial fundamentals, it said.
Sumitomo has accused its former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka of racking up $2.6 billion of losses from unauthorised metals trades.

Moody's said the losses would depress Sumitomo's earnings and financial flexibility but added that despite a substantial drain on Sumitomo's equity, its capital holding remained among the highest of its peers.

Moody's said it would continue to monitor developments concerning Sumitomo's copper trading losses, as the company may be liable for additional contingencies, such as litigation and sanctions by authorities.
